alreadyMinedMarker.why: The loop's last missing arrow. While WATCHING, nothing told you a line was already a card — so you re-mine it and find out from Anki's duplicate warning, after the framing, screenshot and audio clip are all captured. That is exactly what the G-PLAY run hit.
alreadyMinedMarker.how: findMinedCueEntry — pure, over mining history already in the panel's state. No Anki call and no I/O, so it cannot stutter playback. The marker sits beside the mine result, OUTSIDE the collapsible form, so it is legible before any capture work is done.
threeRules: watchLoopSourceKey REFUSES videoCoreResumeKey's `playback:` fallback. A playbackId is a directstream id minted fresh on every open, so it can never establish that a cue was mined in an EARLIER session. Accepting it would make the lookup appear to work — it matches fine within one session, which is precisely when you least need it — and silently answer 'never mined' after every restart.

Cue identity is trackNumber + index + startMs TOGETHER. Index alone is not enough: selecting a track mid-playback restarts the stream and re-indexes from the current position (a real G-PLAY finding), so an index can point at different lines across two sessions. startMs comes from the demuxer and is stable.

`exported` and `duplicate` count as already-mined; `undone` and `failed` do NOT. A duplicate means Anki refused because the note exists. An undone card was deliberately removed, so the line is genuinely minable again — warning there would be wrong in the direction that costs the user a card.

phase6ShellHandoff.theDefect: `video.resumeLast` is a BUILT-IN (slice 11), so it is offered in every shell that mounts CommandPalette — the reader, every pop-out, the desktop. Only some of those mount MediaWorkspaceHost. The app's only test for 'can I hand a file to the player?' was mediaWorkspaceHostIsMounted(), a DOM query for `.seanime-host-launcher`, which answers 'is a host mounted AND has a non-disabled status arrived?'. Measured with the sidecar at `ready` and no host: the toast read 'The media server is off, so there is nothing to resume into.' A missing host is a fact about the WINDOW; a disabled sidecar is a fact about the MACHINE. False by default since the slice-12 flip.
phase6ShellHandoff.secondInstance: A `player` pop-out routes to the workspace (retirement step 2) but App mounted the host only for `popout === 'video'`, so the section's own open button dispatched into a window with no listener. THREE places encode 'which sections open the workspace' — AppSection's switch, the host's os:open listener, App's pop-out mount — and only the third was stale. Now one list: MEDIA_WORKSPACE_SECTIONS / sectionOpensMediaWorkspace(). A pop-out is a separate renderer with its own App tree, so 'the host is mounted' is per-window and cannot be inherited from the desktop that spawned it.
phase6ShellHandoff.presenceIsTheListenersLifetime: MediaWorkspaceHost calls registerMediaWorkspaceHost() from INSIDE the effect that adds its window listeners and releases it in that effect's cleanup. It therefore reports true a full commit BEFORE `status` arrives and the launcher renders — which is exactly the state the reader handoff creates, and exactly where the DOM marker reads false. The release is idempotent because StrictMode runs an effect's cleanup twice and a second decrement would under-count a host that is still mounted.
phase6ShellHandoff.theDomMarkerIsKept: mediaWorkspaceHostIsMounted() still gates the palette's search-mode Continue-watching group and Statistics' By-show rows. Those decide whether to OFFER a list, in the tick they render, with no room for an await — and with the sidecar disabled those rows would open a player the user never sees. Right question there, wrong one for dispatch.
phase6ShellHandoff.threeTrueStatements: no host in this window -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.noWorkspaceHere (new); sidecar disabled -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.unavailable (now only when true, answered by MAIN on the failure path only via a new non-hook mediaWorkspaceIsAvailable() that useMediaWorkspaceAvailability is written in terms of); empty store -> mediaWorkspace.resumeLast.nothing. The shell answer NEVER asks main — that is knowable without the sidecar, and asking anyway would let an IPC failure re-word a shell fact as a sidecar fact. Pinned by asserting statusCalls === 0.
phase6ShellHandoff.readerHandoff: renderer/readerResumeHandoff.ts. While a book is open App registers a handler that checks availability, closes the book, and lets the EFFECT BODY run the ordinary built-in against the desktop that just came back. Availability is checked BEFORE the close so a disabled sidecar never costs the user their book. The resume runs from the effect body rather than the handler so it lands after the commit — MediaWorkspaceHost is a child of the component running the hook and a child's effects run before its parent's, so the listener exists by then, with no sleep and no polling. It lives outside App.tsx so it can be driven against a REAL host rather than a re-creation of the shell.

openGenerationPatch20260801.what: patches/seanime/0004-directstream-open-generation.patch — a client-supplied generation the SIDECAR can refuse, consulted BEFORE BeginOpen. The half of the stale-open problem a client cannot do.
openGenerationPatch20260801.closes: The sentence slices 32, 37 and 39 all end at: a recovery request already sent CANNOT BE RECALLED — fetch abort abandons the response, never the work — so it can land inside a later open and BeginOpen -> beginSubtitleSeek strips that open subtitles. Slice 32 named the only two fixes: a generation the sidecar can reject, or a client rule that never issues while a newer open is outstanding. shared/directstreamOpenChannel.ts is the second; this is the FIRST.

rule.api: Manager.AcceptOpenGeneration(clientId, generation), called before BeginOpen — after it the damage is already done
rule.unspecified: 0, negative, or no client id -> ACCEPTED and records nothing, so every existing client is unaffected
rule.equal: ACCEPTED — a re-open of the SAME request is the legitimate recovery this protects, not a stale one
rule.older: REFUSED, with an error, before BeginOpen runs
rule.other: clients are ordered independently; a refusal does not move the bar

openGenerationPatch20260801.inertOnPurpose: Nothing sends generation — not Study OS, not upstream — so applying the patch changes NO observable behaviour. That is what makes the server half landable and verifiable alone, while the client half (generation: requestId on the open body and on every recovery for that request) stays a separate, live-measured step. For the same reason it is NOT in build-patched-sidecar.mjs patch list; adding it there is the wiring session call.

machineTraps: Git Bash tar cannot extract to a Windows path — git archive | tar -C C:\... fails with "Cannot connect to C: resolve failed" because it reads C: as a remote host. Both tools use git clone instead, which also gives the diff a .git to be taken against. build-patched-sidecar.mjs gets away with tar.exe because that resolves to System32.

git clone honours the global core.autocrlf, so the tree comes out CRLF, every multi-line anchor stops matching, and a patch generated from it would carry line-ending churn into an upstream-submittable diff. Both tools clone and check out with -c core.autocrlf=false. Slice 39 CRLF lesson arriving from a completely different direction on the same day.
